neutral.why: Open circle-gap eyes tracking level plus a flat, uncurved line mouth — no smile, no frown, the resting default face.

happy.why: Wide circle-gap eyes over a solid filled smile-bowl mouth (~1.9:1 wide, a real grin shape, not just a curved line) — an unambiguous big smile.

sad.why: Open eyes over a downward n-shaped frown arc plus a single streaming tear — sorrow, not just a flat mouth.

alert.why: Wide open C-shaped eyes (no droop, no lid closure) paired with a flat closed line mouth — watching hard, mouth uncommitted.

bored.why: Heavy closed-lid arcs drooping shut over a flat, unmoved line mouth — eyes half checked-out, nothing left to say.

dead_inside.why: Closed crescent 'smiling' happy-arc eyes paired with literally no mouth at all — a smile-shape with nothing underneath reads as hollowed-out.

error.why: The two eyes are mismatched shapes (one flat-topped C, one near-perfect circular arc) and the mouth is a single line tilted ~15° off-axis — asymmetric, glitched geometry reads as a fault state.

smug.why: Squared bracket-shaped '⊐⊏' eyes plus a smile-arc tilted ~7° higher on one side than the other — a lopsided smirk, not a symmetric grin.

curious.why: Wide open circle-gap eyes fixed on something, with only a tiny 'o' dot mouth (~15% of eye diameter) — leaning in, mouth barely reacting yet.

sleepy.why: Shallow closed-lid arcs (upturned, drooping-shut eyes) plus a tall filled oval mouth (height ~1.45x its width) — a face caught mid-yawn.

angry.why: Open hook-shaped angry eyes with a sharp inward slant over a downturned frown arc — direct, unmistakable anger.

love.why: Closed crescent happy-arc eyes with a soft, flat closed mouth (no bared grin needed) — reads as a warm, doting smile rather than an open laugh.

suspicious.why: Narrow closed chevron-slit eyes over a flat, pursed capsule mouth — guarded and unconvinced, lips held shut.

surprised.why: Wide, spiral letter-shaped eyes thrown open plus a tall open-O mouth — the whole face has popped wide open.

panic.why: Wide open C-shaped eyes over a wavering w-squiggle mouth (a trembling stroke, not a smooth curve) — reads as frantic distress, not amusement.

listening.why: Open circle-gap eyes held steady on the speaker plus a small closed dot mouth — quiet, receptive, not talking.

thinking.why: The two eyes are mirror-opposite letter shapes (left eye reversed, right standard) — looking inward rather than straight ahead — over a small closed pursed mouth: turning something over mentally.

mischief.why: Closed crescent happy-arc eyes with a squiggly cat/omega mouth (the classic ':3' curve) — a sly, impish grin.

proud.why: Direct open circle-gap eyes over a broad open smile-arc — chin-up and confident, looking straight out.

embarrassed.why: Inward-pointing '>' and '<' chevron eyes squeezed toward the center over a flat underscore mouth — the classic flustered '>_<' scrunch.
